title: 2015 HMMT November Guts Problem 14
statement: Let \(A B C\) be an acute triangle with orthocenter \(H\). Let \(D, E\) be the feet of the \(A, B\)-altitudes respectively. Given that \(A H=20\) and \(H D=15\) and \(B E=56\), find the length of \(B H\).

solutions.text:
Answer: 50
Let \(x\) be the length of \(B H\). Note that quadrilateral \(A B D E\) is cyclic, so by Power of a Point, \(x(56-x)=\) \(20 \cdot 15=300\). Solving for \(x\), we get \(x=50\) or 6 . We must have \(B H>H D\) so \(x=50\) is the correct length.
